newsitem.title: FRANCE: Yves Saint Laurent head gets suspended sentence.
newsitem.headline: Yves Saint Laurent head gets suspended sentence.

text.p: A Paris court gave Pierre Berge, ex-director of the Bastille Opera and now head of the Yves Saint Laurent fashion house, a 10-month suspended sentence on Thursday for the fatal collapse of a rehearsal set in Seville, Spain.
Berge was accused of failing to take steps which could have prevented the accident in 1992 in which a member of the opera chorus, Annick Taffary, was killed and 39 singers and technicians were hurt.
Found guilty by the court of manslaughter Berge was also fined 30,000 francs ($6,000) for failing to set up a safety committee.
The set collapsed when the Bastille opera company was rehearsing for a performance of Verdi's "Otello" as part of Seville's Expo 92 exhibition cultural programme.
During the mid-November trial, a lawyer for Taffary's relatives accused the opera company and top officials of making petty savings on safety and imprudently rushing a production.

In the same case, former Bastille Opera technical director Jean-Michel Dubois received a 15-month suspended jail term while then-general manager Georges-Francois Hirsch was given a suspended sentence of eight months.
Both men were also fined 30,000 francs ($6,000).
